verdict.line: You lose the poke war before level 6, but you win the lane and the duel once Unstoppable Force comes online (50.7% over 1341 games).

brief.thesis: Urgot's Corrosive Charge (800 range) outranges every tool Malphite has pre-6, so the early lane is a poke tax you have to eat. Once R (Unstoppable Force) hits level 6, Malphite gets an engage Disdain can't stop and an E that guts Urgot's auto-attack-reliant Purge, which is why the sample swings to Malphite's favor and OP.GG's own read says to go for kills after 6.

theirWindow.what: Urgot pokes with Corrosive Charge (800 range, 10-8s cooldown) and autos while you have no ranged answer. Only trade when Granite Shield has recharged, and don't push to the edge of his Q range just to land your own Q.

yourWindow.what: Charge in with Unstoppable Force — it knocks him up and can't be stopped by Disdain's flip. Follow with Brutal Strikes for the cleave and Armor/AD buff, and Ground Slam to cut his attack speed before Purge can unload.

start.why: The 76.8% pick rate and 51.2% win rate reflect mana regen and early AP that keep your Ground Slam and Seismic Shard trades up without forcing recalls through Urgot's poke.

boots.why: 84.1% pick, 51.6% win rate — Urgot's damage is almost entirely basic attacks (Purge, Echoing Flames passive, autos), so flat auto-attack reduction directly cuts his trade and all-in damage.

core.why: Highest-winning path start (60.8% over 79 games) — health and armor to soak Q poke while the burn aura adds pressure in extended trades.
Punishes Urgot's auto-attack-heavy Purge and passive with return damage and Grievous Wounds, which matters most since his kit lives on repeated autos.
Stacks attack speed reduction on top of your Ground Slam, further strangling Urgot's Purge DPS while adding armor and mana.

runes.keystoneWhy: 13.4% pick, 49.1% win rate — rewards the proactive melee trading Malphite wants here (walk up, auto, cleave with W) and the healing offsets the chip damage from Urgot's poke.

summoners.why: This combo posts the highest measured win rate (53.4%) and matches the matchup's real pattern — solo-kill advantage after level 6 that Ignite helps close out. Flash+Teleport is far more popular (77.5% pick) if you'd rather prioritize wave resets and scaling over early kill pressure.

playing.title: Trade only with shield recharged
playing.detail: Granite Shield only matters if you haven't been hit recently — walk into extended trades only when it's visibly back up, not right after eating a Q.

playing.title: Respect the 800-range Q
playing.detail: Corrosive Charge outranges your Seismic Shard (625) and both your melee abilities (400). Don't creep forward to land your own poke; let him come to you.

playing.title: Time Ground Slam before his Purge
playing.detail: E's attack speed reduction directly cuts the DPS of Purge and the procs on Echoing Flames — land it right before he channels, not after.

playing.title: Save R for clean, unstoppable engages
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force can't be interrupted by Disdain's flip, so look for moments he's pushed up or out of position rather than using it purely on reaction.

playing.title: Max Q first, E second, W last
playing.detail: The measured skill order (QEWQQRQEQEREEWW) prioritizes Seismic Shard for wave pressure and kiting denial, then Ground Slam for the attack-speed shred, leaving Brutal Strikes for last.

playing.title: All-in starts at 6, not before
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read and the solo-kill numbers agree: don't force fights pre-6 when you're behind on range. Once R is up, that's your window to kill him.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample numbers above come from measured Malphite vs. Urgot games on the current patch (OP.GG); the tactical reasoning — why each pick works and when to use each ability — is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid Urgot’s (Q) pokes and his (E)-(R) combo while laning! Try to kill him after reaching level 6.
